title: Commercial Property Secretary
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Macildowie are working with this client based in Leicester to recruit an experienced Legal Secretary to join their Commercial Property team.

Legal Secretary - Commercial Property

Location: Leicester
Salary: £30000
Contract: Permanent
Working Arrangement: Hybrid and Flexible

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established professional services organisation, providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support to a busy team of property specialists.

You'll be working closely with fee earners, helping to ensure commercial property matters progress smoothly and clients receive a professional and responsive service. It's a varied position where organisation, accuracy and the ability to juggle competing priorities will be key.

What will you be doing?

You'll provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support, including:
- Creating, formatting and amending legal documents and correspondence
- Producing accurate documentation from digital dictation
- Preparing leases, reports and other property-related documents
- Managing diaries, meetings and day-to-day administration for fee earners
- Opening, maintaining and closing client and matter files
- Liaising professionally with clients, agents, solicitors and other external parties
- Supporting commercial property transactions with searches and documentation
- Assisting with Land Registry and Companies House documentation
- Supporting Stamp Duty Land Tax returns, completion paperwork and post-completion administration
- Assisting fee earners with time recording, billing and routine accounting queries
- Scanning, printing and preparing documentation for signature

What are we looking for?

You'll be highly organised, accurate and comfortable working in a fast-paced professional environment.

Previous legal secretarial experience would be highly desirable, with experience supporting Commercial Property or Real Estate teams particularly advantageous.

You'll also need:
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Strong written and verbal communication
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good IT literacy and confidence learning new systems
- Experience working with document and/or case management systems
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
- A professional and client-focused approach

If you're an experienced Legal Secretary looking for your next opportunity in Leicester, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Please apply with your latest CV for further information.

Macildowie is a specialist recruitment consultancy with a rich history of enhancing the careers of professionals across the Midlands and Northern Home Counties. We have an unrivalled understanding of the local market and are dedicated to helping you achieve your career aspirations.

title: Accounts Payable Co-ordinator
description:
Accounts Payable Coordinator

Fleckney

Full time, Permanent

Monday - Friday

£27,000 per annum

We are working with a well-established and successful
organisation, who are looking for an experienced Accounts Payable
Coordinator to join their Finance team. Reporting to the Accounts
Payable Supervisor, this role will be responsible for managing
the Accounts Payable function across multiple group companies,
ensuring invoices, payments and supplier accounts are processed
accurately and efficiently.

You will play a key role in maintaining strong supplier
relationships, resolving queries, processing multi-currency
payments and ensuring all Accounts Payable records remain
accurate and up to date.

Key Responsibilities for an Accounts Payable Coordinator:

Manage the Accounts Payable function across multiple group
companies
Process and match supplier invoices, ensuring correct
authorisation
Reconcile supplier statements and resolve queries
Liaise with internal teams and international suppliers
Process high-value and multi-currency payments, including BACS
and one-off payments
Accurately allocate payments and maintain cash book records
Support cashflow forecasting and maintain future payment
records
Monitor the Accounts Payable inbox and respond to supplier
queries
Maintain and reconcile GRNI and Preliminary Invoice reports
Provide general administration and team cover when required

Key Skills for an Accounts Payable Coordinator:

Minimum 3 years' experience within an Accounts Payable
environment
Strong knowledge of end-to-end Accounts Payable processes
Experience processing high-value and high-volume payments
Previous experience dealing with multiple currencies
Strong Excel skills and good general IT knowledge
Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
Strong communication and relationship-building skills
Excellent organisational and time management skills

If the above is of interest to you, we'd love to hear from you,
apply today!

title: Part Time Accounts Assistant
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Part-Time Accounts Assistant Leicester City Centre Hybrid Temporary Ongoing Up to £16.00ph

Macildowie are working with a fantastic business based in Leicester City Centre looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join their finance team on an ongoing temporary basis.

The key details:
- Up to £16.00ph, depending on experience
- 3-4 days per week
- Flexible on working days and hours
- Hybrid working
- Leicester City Centre
- ASAP start - ideally next week
- Temporary ongoing position
- Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central experience is highly desirable, although not essential

This is a varied, hands-on transactional finance position covering both Purchase Ledger and Sales Ledger, alongside wider accounts administration.

Day-to-day duties will include:
- Processing purchase invoices and maintaining the Accounts Payable ledger
- Supplier statement reconciliations and resolving queries
- Raising and posting Sales Ledger invoices
- Processing credit cards and employee expenses
- Managing and reconciling foreign currency bank accounts
- Supporting general bank and balance sheet reconciliations
- Managing the shared finance mailbox
- Dealing with internal and external finance queries
- Supporting the wider finance team with general transactional accounting duties

We are looking for someone with previous Accounts Assistant / Finance Assistant / Purchase Ledger / Sales Ledger experience who can confidently pick up a varied workload and get up to speed quickly.

Experience using Microsoft Business Central would be a real advantage, but candidates with strong transactional finance experience using similar accounting systems will also be considered.

If you are available at short notice and looking for a flexible part-time opportunity, please apply or get in touch for more information.

title: Casualty Claims Handler
description:
A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims on behalf of a number of Public Sector clients.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.
- Due to growth and expansion this will be an exciting time to join where you will be offered the opportunity to progress and develop long-term.

Key responsibilities:
- Handle a variety of casualty/personal injury claims through to settlement
- Verify policy cover/validity
- Log and record all claims digitally
- Investigate allocated claims either from desk or instructed by the team of loss adjusters
- Where appropriate refer to a field adjuster for site investigation to establish how the loss occurred
- Gather all necessary evidence and relevant documentation
- Determine appropriate action for resolution
- Make decision on liability and negotiate settlement where appropriate
- Keep up to date with any technical changes within the industry and to your role which may involve participating in training programmes within the company

About you:
- Liability/Casualty Claims handling experience working in the Loss Adjusting, Insurance or Legal Sector
- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- The ability or understand insurance policy wordings and the insurance market
- Knowledge of civil procedure rules and the claims portal
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on Offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

title: Mental Health Act Administrator
description: Are you an experienced Mental Health Act Administrator with a passion for ensuring legal compliance and supporting excellent patient care? Elizabeth House is looking for a dedicated and organised Mental Health Act (MHA) Administrator to join our multidisciplinary team. This is an exciting opportunity to play a vital role in ensuring that all Mental Health Act processes are managed accurately, efficiently, and in accordance with statutory requirements. As our MHA Administrator, you will work closely with the Hospital Director, Responsible Clinicians, nursing teams, and external agencies to ensure the hospital maintains the highest standards of legal compliance and governance. You will be responsible for the administration of all aspects of the Mental Health Act 1983 (as amended), ensuring legal documentation is accurate, compliant, and processed within statutory timescales. You will provide expert advice to staff, coordinate Mental Health Tribunal and Hospital Managers' Hearings, maintain legal records, and support the organisation during CQC inspections and internal audits. Key Responsibilities Administer all Mental Health Act documentation in line with current legislation and the Mental Health Act Code of Practice. Scrutinise detention papers for legal accuracy and identify any anomalies. Maintain the Mental Health Act Tracker and monitor statutory deadlines, renewals, consent to treatment requirements, and appeals. Coordinate Mental Health Tribunals and Hospital Managers' Hearings. Liaise with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), Tribunal Service, Responsible Clinicians, Independent Hospital Managers, IMHAs, and other stakeholders. Ensure statutory rights are explained and appropriate documentation is provided to patients. Maintain secure legal files and ensure clinical records are updated appropriately. Complete monthly audits of Mental Health Act documentation and legal files. Produce governance reports and compliance data. Provide advice and guidance to staff on Mental Health Act processes. Support the delivery of Mental Health Act training across the service.
